title: Elucidating the Mechanisms of Chrysanthemum Action on Atopic Dermatitis via Network Pharmacology and Machine Learning.
authors: Li, Shiying; Jiang, Yongxin; Hu, Chengxiang; Ding, Yiyao; Fu, Xueqi; Xing, Shu; Zeng, Linlin
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过网络药理学和机器学习探究菊花治疗特应性皮炎的作用机制，核心是药物-靶点-疾病网络，而非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅涉及分子对接模拟，与本课题关联度低。
abstract: Chrysanthemum (Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat.) has been recognized as both a food and medicinal substance in China since 2002 and possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and immunomodulatory activities. Previous studies suggest that Chrysanthemum may alleviate skin lesions resembling atopic dermatitis (AD); however, its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we integrated network pharmacology and machine learning to systematically explore the potential mechanisms of Chrysanthemum in AD treatment. Four algorithms-Random Forest (RF), Lasso regression with cross-validation (LassoCV), Elastic Net (EN), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB)-were compared, among which the XGB model achieved the best performance (accuracy = 0.9393). Further analysis identified 15 optimal features, two core targets (PTGS2 and MMP9), and one critical pathway (NF-kappaB signaling). To experimentally validate these findings, HaCaT keratinocytes were co-stimulated with TNF-alpha and IFN-gamma to establish an in vitro inflammatory model, and co-treatment with three major flavonoids from Chrysanthemum-Acacetin, Diosmetin, and Chryseriol-significantly suppressed cytokine-induced COX-2 overexpression and reduced NF-kappaB p65 phosphorylation, confirming their inhibitory effects on NF-kappaB activation. These results were consistent with molecular docking and dynamics simulations, which demonstrated that these flavonoids, along with celecoxib, could stably bind to COX-2, thereby enhancing system stability and reducing residue fluctuations at the binding interface, revealing the molecular basis by which Chrysanthemum alleviates AD and supporting its modernization and therapeutic potential.
abstract_zh: 菊花（Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat.）自2002年起在中国被认定为药食同源物质，具有抗氧化、抗炎、抗菌及免疫调节活性。既往研究表明，菊花可能缓解类似特应性皮炎（atopic dermatitis, AD）的皮肤病变；然而，其潜在机制尚不明确。在本研究中，我们整合网络药理学和机器学习，系统探索菊花治疗AD的潜在机制。比较了四种算法——随机森林（Random Forest, RF）、带交叉验证的Lasso回归（LassoCV）、弹性网络（Elastic Net, EN）和极端梯度提升（Extreme Gradient Boosting, XGB）——其中XGB模型表现最佳（准确率 = 0.9393）。进一步分析识别出15个最优特征、两个核心靶点（PTGS2和MMP9）以及一条关键通路（NF-kappaB信号通路）。为实验验证这些发现，用TNF-alpha和IFN-gamma共刺激HaCaT角质形成细胞以建立体外炎症模型，并与菊花中三种主要黄酮类化合物——金合欢素（Acacetin）、香叶木素（Diosmetin）和芹菜素（Chryseriol）共处理，显著抑制了细胞因子诱导的COX-2过表达，并减少NF-kappaB p65磷酸化，证实了它们对NF-kappaB激活的抑制作用。这些结果与分子对接和动力学模拟一致，表明这些黄酮类化合物以及塞来昔布（celecoxib）能稳定结合COX-2，从而增强系统稳定性并减少结合界面处的残基波动，揭示了菊花缓解AD的分子基础，并支持其现代化及治疗潜力。
